# Deck slide map and short scripts (auto-generated by v2_reflective/build_deck_clean.py on every build; do not edit)

Same text as the PowerPoint / Google Slides speaker notes. Longer scripts: `Presenter_Notes.md`, Part 0.

| Slide | Title | Short script (speaker note) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Agentic Self-Correction in LLaMA-3 | Title. Say: we take a published LLM method for rating product reviews, rebuild it and study it, then build our own agent-based approach on top of what we learn. |
| 2 | The reference paper in a nutshell | The reference paper. Wang et al. (2025), ITM Web of Conferences 70, 04021. Say: we chose this paper as our reference. Task: rate an Amazon product review 1-5 stars with a short justification. Approach: one fine-tuned LLaMA-3-8B reads the review once. Data: Kaggle Amazon reviews, about 500K. It reports 92.6% accuracy and 93.3% F1 with 5-fold cross-validation and a 40K-review test set, and beats SVM, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree and XLNet. |
| 3 | Its stack | The paper's stack. Data: TextBlob quality control drops reviews whose tone contradicts the star; stratified sampling balances the stars; VGST, a greedy diversity search, prefers reviews with new words; 3-star reviews are doubled. Model: LLaMA-3-8B in 4-bit, LoRA rank 4, alpha 64 on the last 3 layers, 3 epochs; fits one 16 GB GPU. Prompt: a 1-5 star rubric, one worked example and a step-by-step cue. Output: a star and a justification. |
| 4 | How we implemented it | Implementation. We rebuilt the pipeline with the paper's Table 1 settings. As a check, on the paper's own data source (Kaggle, its protocol, no leak) it reaches 69.1%; always guessing 5 stars already gives 63.8% there. Then a clean benchmark: Amazon Reviews 2023 Electronics, splits drawn once and kept disjoint (train about 497K, development, balanced test 1,000, natural test 2,000); every choice made on development data; test sets read once. |
| 5 | Right direction, wrong star | Phase 1 results (results_frozen.md). The reference method on Electronics, leak-free: exact star 54.0% balanced, 53.4% natural; within one star 93.7% / 94.4%. It reads the direction well; choosing between neighbouring stars is the hard part. The paper's 92.6% used a different protocol and is not comparable. |
| 6 | Four things hold it back | Findings. (1) Label leak (LOG 2026-10-11): in our first reproduction the prompt's example hinted at the answer; a random example costs 7.7 points. This was our first reproduction's example choice, not a claim about the authors. (2) TextBlob cleaning removes 52% of 1-star and 67% of 2-star reviews. (3) Justifications are a template: 5 distinct sentences for 150 reviews, none quoting the review (x1_explain_compare.out). (4) One model, one pass: nothing catches a mistake. |
| 7 | Its novelty | What the paper contributes, and why we chose it: (1) a general open LLM fine-tuned for five-star rating, beating classic models and XLNet; (2) a data pipeline combining quality control, balance, lexical diversity and neutral oversampling; (3) parameter-efficient training, a small LoRA add-on and 4-bit weights on one 16 GB GPU; (4) a prompt that returns a justification with the star. Our findings show where each of these needs help. |
| 8 | Our approach | Our approach. Say: from Part 1 we need a second opinion, data kept whole, and explanations that can be checked. Three attempts to let an LLM decide the star failed, so trained models decide, the LLM explains, and checks keep the explanation honest. |
| 9 | Our stack | Our stack. Three independent agents read the review: the LLaMA probe (a classifier on a frozen LLaMA-3-8B layer, meaning), the Evidence model (TF-IDF + logistic regression on about 497K reviews, key words) and DeBERTa-v3 (fine-tuned encoder, wording). The Reflector, a logistic regression on their probabilities, decides the star. The Hand-off agent answers only when confident. The Explainer writes from the evidence; the Critic checks it and sends it back, up to four rewrites. Built in LangGraph; LLaMA runs locally on MLX. |
| 10 | Why it works | Why several agents beat one (agents_complement.png). Left: the Evidence model wins on short reviews, the LLaMA probe on long reviews, and the combined stack is best or near-best in every length band. Right: when the probe and the Evidence model disagree, the stack still gets 58-62% right, against 36-50% for either alone. The Reflector learns which agent to trust for which review. |
| 11 | What we tried and dropped | Approaches tried (EXPERIMENTS_SUMMARY.md, section 3). Every idea had a pass/fail rule written before it ran and was checked on development data only; none touched the test sets. LLM deciding the star: 54.2% vs 73.3% on disagreement rows, and later 76 fixed vs 89 broken. Product-photo agent: constant output. More views of the same text (MiniLM, character n-grams, NB-SVM): no gain. Bigger LLaMA probe (120K): +0.3, saturated. Gradient-boosted Reflector: overfits (.621 vs .642). Second LLM judge: rejects everything. |
| 12 | What we kept, and why | What we kept (EXPERIMENTS_SUMMARY.md, section 2; LOG). Leak-free zero-shot protocol (the leak was 7.7 points). Raw balanced data: TextBlob filtering cost 2.5-3.5 points. LLaMA probe on 40K reviews: +3.9 on dev2. Evidence model on about 497K reviews. DeBERTa-v3: +2.3 on the natural test, stable over 3 seeds. Logistic-regression Reflector. Critic loop up to four rewrites: 0 broken. Hand-off agent. |
| 13 | +24.6 points | Hero moment. Pause on the number. Say: on the natural mix of reviews, the three-agent system gets the exact star 24.6 points more often than the reference method (53.4% to 78.0%); on balanced reviews +13.5 (54.0% to 67.5%). Both significant after Holm correction (analysis_C.out). Then go to the chart. |
| 14 | Phase 2 gets the exact star far more often | Headline (results_frozen.md, analysis_C.out). Exact star: Phase 1 54.0 / 53.4, Phase 2 67.5 / 78.0: +13.5 and +24.6 points, 29% and 53% fewer errors, significant after Holm correction. Within one star 97.3 / 97.4. If asked whether 67.5 is good: random is 20%, and neighbouring stars are ambiguous. Caveat if asked: on balanced eval the three-agent stack ties the previous two-agent stack; DeBERTa's +2.3 is on the natural mix. |
| 15 | Negative words, happy reviewer | Hard cases (hard_cases.out). Reviews whose words sound negative but whose star is 4 or 5. Phase 1: 35.0% (balanced, n 40), 43.0% (natural, n 193). Phase 2: 67.5% and 78.2%. p 0.0023 and 5.4e-16. |
| 16 | It knows when it is unsure | Hand-off agent (s1_selective.out). Threshold fixed on dev2 before the tests. Natural test: answers 56% of reviews automatically, 92.8% right. Balanced test: 86.9% on 41%; Phase 1 with the same rule 66.9%. What it hands to a person is only 54-59% right: those are the hard ones. Star ranges (q1_conformal.out): a range that holds the true star 90% of the time is 1.44 stars wide on natural (Phase 1 2.08). |
| 17 | Its explanations are checked and faithful | Critic loop (b2_report.out). The Critic checks five things: the star matches, every quote is in the review, it uses the key phrases, it mentions disagreement, and an LLM judge finds no invented claim. Faithful first drafts 62.3% / 63.7%; after up to four rewrites 90.5% / 91.6%; 841 fixed, 0 broken. Deletion test: removing the cited words lowers confidence about twice as much as removing random words (0.156 vs 0.077 balanced). |
| 18 | One review, three drafts | Worked example from the live demo (presentation/demo_cache.json, balanced test). Read the review, then the drafts: the Critic names what is wrong (an invented phrase, too few key phrases) and draft 3 passes all checks. Phase 1's justification for comparison is a template that never quotes the review. |
| 19 | A person checked the Critic | Human check (human_check.out, LOG 2026-11-20). The author marked 50 random explanations, blind to the Critic: 80% faithful vs the Critic's 92%, agreement 76%. When all agents agreed (34) the author passed every one; when they disagreed (16) only 37.5%, while the Critic passed 93.8%. There the Explainer says things about the system ("the reviewer gave N stars", a confidence %) that no check catches. One annotator, 50 items: an indication. |
| 20 | Stable on messy text, but it needs the title | Robustness (q4_robustness.out, 300 balanced reviews). Share of reviews whose star changes when the text is changed. Typos: 0.7% vs 2.0% (ns). No punctuation or capitals: 9.3% vs 29.7%. Title removed: 15.7% vs 0%, because the Evidence model and DeBERTa read the title. Say the limitation plainly. |
| 21 | Phase 1 vs Phase 2, side by side | Why it is better: every row is a number already shown. Exact star 54.0 to 67.5 (balanced) and 53.4 to 78.0 (natural). Negative-sounding happy reviews 35.0 to 67.5. Explanations that quote the review 0% to 75.3% (x1_explain_compare.out). When sure: 66.9% to 86.9% right on about 41% of balanced reviews. Star changes on flat text 29.7% to 9.3%. One thing is worse: without the title, 0% to 15.7%. |
| 22 | What the project shows | Conclusion. (1) The reference method, rebuilt leak-free, gets 54% exact; we found a label leak, a cleaning step that removes negative reviews, and template justifications. (2) Three agents and a Reflector reach 67.5% / 78.0%, +13.5 / +24.6 points, significant. (3) The agentic layer makes the output checkable: 91-92% faithful explanations, 0 broken; 93% right when it answers alone; a human check shows where the Critic is still too lenient. Limits: one dataset; needs the title. |
